newsitem.title: UK: Police enquiry into $2.5m Heathrow theft continues.
newsitem.headline: Police enquiry into $2.5m Heathrow theft continues.

text.p: No arrests have yet been made in relation to the theft of about $2.5 million of U.S. aid destined for Russia at Heathrow airport last week but police enquiries were continuing on Monday, a police spokeswoman said.

The stolen money was in the process of being transferred between a British Airways' World Cargo warehouse at Heathrow and a BA Boeing 767 passenger aircraft between 7.45 and 8.15 am on February 25. Contained in a canvas bag, it was reported missing at 8.30 am.
The missing bag was one of four containing a total of about $10 million being transferred between banks and which was en route to Moscow.

The spokeswoman said police were unaware of the names of the banks involved, although UK press reports said the money came from the Republic National Bank of New York and was being sent to the Moscow-based Toko Bank as part of U.S. aid funding for the Russian economy.
A BA spokesman said on Monday that he understood these were the banks involved.
The investigation was being conducted by Heathrow police's Criminal Investigation Department, the New Scotland Yard spokeswoman said.
The BA spokesman said the airline reported the disappearance of the money promptly to the police and had since then been co-operating fully.
"There are no further developments. It is an ongoing police investgation," he said.
